LESSON: USE OF TOILET HYGIENE

Grade: Grade 1
Subject: HYGIENE AND NUTRITION ACTIVITIES
Strand: Personal
Topic 2.1: Use of toilet Hygiene

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Use of toilet Hygiene. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: USE OF TOILET HYGIENE
Subject: HYGIENE AND NUTRITION ACTIVITIES · Grade: Grade 1
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Use of toilet Hygiene helps you succeed in HYGIENE AND NUTRITION ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS: USE OF TOILET HYGIENE
Use of toilet Hygiene is part of Science learning. Connect every idea to something you can observe.
Use safe examples only. Do not try dangerous experiments without a teacher.
Write definitions in your own words, then add one drawing or real-life example.

PART 1: Name materials used to clean (sponges, pumice stone, face towel, 2.

What this means
In this part you learn to name materials used to clean (sponges, pumice stone, face towel, 2.. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: name materials used to clean (sponges, pumice stone, face towel, 2..
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Use of toilet Hygiene” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can name materials used to clean (sponges, pumice stone, face towel, 2.. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Appreciate the importance of a materials without waste (soap, water, clean body for personal toothpast

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the importance of a materials without waste (soap, water, clean body for personal toothpast. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the importance of a materials without waste (soap, water, clean body for personal toothpast.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Say why Use of toilet Hygiene matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the importance of a materials without waste (soap, water, clean body for personal toothpast. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Use of toilet Hygiene is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Use of toilet Hygiene” around your school. (skill: name materials used to clean (sponges, pumice stone, face towel, 2.)

Example 2: Say why Use of toilet Hygiene matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya. (skill: appreciate the importance of a materials without waste (soap, water, clean body for personal toothpast)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Use of toilet Hygiene to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: name materials used to clean (sponges, pumice stone, face towel, 2..
3. Practise this skill: appreciate the importance of a materials without waste (soap, water, clean body for personal toothpast.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Use of toilet Hygiene from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Use of toilet Hygiene: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 1 learner study Use of toilet Hygiene?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why do we clean our hygiene parts of the body learner should be able to: used to clean parts of the body bodies?
2. how to clean parts of without waste?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Use of toilet Hygiene means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: name materials used to clean (sponges, pumice stone, face towel, 2..
5. Be able to: appreciate the importance of a materials without waste (soap, water, clean body for personal toothpast.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.
